title: Cell Phone-Induced Failures of Visual Attention During Driving

lines.text: Surprisingly, talking on a hands-free phone while driving can impair your reaction to brake lights.
Researchers had drivers simulate driving and chat on a phone.
Drivers missed seeing brake lights in front of them.
This happened because they paid less attention to the visual scene.
Eye-tracking showed reduced focus on the road.
Impaired memory for billboards supported this finding.
This means reduced attention to visual inputs impairs driving performance.

sources: Strayer DL, Drews FA, Johnston WA (2003). Cell phone-induced failures of visual attention during simulated driving. J Exp Psychol Appl 9(1):23-32. PMID 12710835
